title: Can 2 People Really Restart Humanity?
analysis_notes: Downloaded on the Spark at 854x480 30fps (format 397 + opus 251, 14 MB, kept) to ~/studio/refs/whatif/6oZ9fdM0n50.mp4 with info.json, webp thumbnail and English auto-subs (json3). Fresh metadata at 09:21 UTC: 4,223,768 views, 27,996 likes (0.66% like rate), 1,900 comments, 12 days after upload, on a 14.1K-sub channel, so roughly 300x its sub count. The description lists chapters (12) and a 'Sources' list of 9 papers/records; the tags are long-tail search phrases ('could 2 people repopulate earth', 'minimum viable population', 'Habsburg jaw', 'black robin Old Blue'). The transcript is from the YouTube auto-subs: 932 spoken words from 1.2 s to 388.6 s. The full timestamped transcript is at research/library/transcripts/6oZ9fdM0n50.txt. There are two voices: a calm narrator, plus short character lines marked '>>' ('So, it's just us?', 'Oh, no.', 'You should have made more friends.'). Background music runs under the whole video; silencedetect found only 3 gaps over 0.6 s (95.6 s, 118.5 s, 239.0 s), each at a section turn. Frames were sampled every 2 s (209 frames). The contact sheet is a 10x21 grid at 160x90. Style: a flat vector 2.5D illustrated world with soft gradients, volumetric light shafts, bloom and film grain. The characters are minimalist 'bean-head' stick people: black circle heads with big white eyes, thin black limbs and coloured tops. The male lead wears a white tee and the female lead a yellow jacket. Only 17 hard cuts were detected (scene > 0.25). Most transitions are continuous camera moves (push-in/pull-out), cross-dissolves and in-scene morphs, so each 'set' lives 10-40 s while overlays change every 2-4 s. Recurring UI: a rounded dark 'pill' caption chip for the key fact (bottom-centre), a dark stat counter box top-left/right with a tiny uppercase label ('POPULATION', 'BLACK ROBINS LEFT', 'NEW MUTATIONS', 'BREEDING ADULTS (EST.)'), a calendar-tab year badge top-right ('YEAR 5', '1516-1700', '+75 YEARS', '1790'), and a tiny source citation bottom-left on every factual claim. Do not reuse the characters, café set, wording or the 'only 2 left' story beats.
title_pattern: 'Can 2 People Really Restart Humanity?' = feasibility question + tiny number + huge stake. Pattern: 'Can [absurdly small N] [ordinary thing] Really [civilisation-scale outcome]?' The digit '2' sets up the scale contrast (2 vs 8 billion), and 'Really' implies the viewer has heard it is possible and invites a skeptic/debunk click. The verb 'Restart' frames humanity as a machine with a reset button. Search tags cover the 'could 2 people repopulate earth' query. The thumbnail does NOT repeat the title ('ONLY 2 LEFT'), so title and thumbnail each add information. Reusable: 'Can 10 People Really Run a Country?', 'Could 1 Person Really Survive on Mars?', 'How Many People Does It Take to Restart Civilization?'.

thumbnail.source: Custom 1280x720 illustration (not a video frame), same art style as the video. Saved to research/library/thumbs/6oZ9fdM0n50.jpg.
thumbnail.composition: High-angle 3/4 view down an empty European street at dusk, with a strong diagonal vanishing point running from bottom-left to top-centre. The two tiny characters stand dead centre in a pool of warm streetlight and cast long shadows toward the camera. Big text sits top-left/centre above their heads. A blurred foreground balcony (bottom-left) and streetlamp (right) frame the shot and give depth.
thumbnail.text: 'ONLY 2 LEFT' in 2 lines, in a heavy rounded geometric sans, all caps, cream/off-white. The '2' is in saturated yellow/gold, the only coloured word. 3 words.
thumbnail.colours: Cool desaturated violet/indigo street and buildings against warm amber light (streetlamp glow, lit café window, a red-white striped awning). Classic complementary purple/orange, with yellow used for the number and the woman's jacket.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: The 2 characters fill less than 15% of the frame inside a large, empty, closed-shutter street. Smallness and isolation ARE the message. Their faces read clearly anyway: big round white eyes, worried brows, small mouths.
thumbnail.why_it_works: It explains the premise in 3 words plus 1 image (an empty city and a couple). The yellow '2' links to the yellow jacket and to the '2' in the title. Worried faces add emotion. Empty everyday places (a café, a street) make the end of the world feel relatable instead of epic. The warm-cool lighting looks premium and stands out from the cluttered red-arrow thumbnails of the science-explainer niche. It is still readable at small size: big text, centred subjects.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: [music] You wake up on a Monday and something is wrong. No traffic, no sirens...
hook.verbatim_0_30s: You wake up on a Monday and something is wrong. No traffic, no sirens, no neighbor drilling into the wall at 7:00 a.m. Overnight, every person on Earth has vanished. Well, almost every person. [character] So, it's just us? [narrator] Which means the entire future of the human species now rests on two strangers who met about 40 seconds ago.
hook.device: Second-person cold open ('You wake up...'), with the setting built from ABSENCES of familiar sounds (traffic, sirens, neighbour's drill). Each absence gets its own visual: a green light with no cars, an ambulance, an empty window. Then comes the premise reveal ('every person has vanished'), a comic correction ('Well, almost every person') and a meet-cute with the second survivor. A stopwatch overlay counting '00:40' makes the joke 'met about 40 seconds ago' land, raising the stakes with humour. The title card arrives at 0:30 as the question 'COULD 2 PEOPLE ACTUALLY REPOPULATE EARTH? ...seriously?' with the word spelled in toy letter blocks. Hook length is about 30 s before the first content beat (8 billion target) at 0:38.
hook.first_frame: The male lead steps out of a dark doorway numbered '12' onto a dusk street next to the café. Mid-action, so there is no static title.

beats.summary: Second-person scenario: you wake on a Monday, and the city is silent (no traffic, sirens, drilling); everyone has vanished. Quick cutaways show each missing sound.

'Well, almost every person': a second survivor appears at the café corner. A character line ('So, it's just us?') and the stakes: humanity's future rests on two strangers who met 40 seconds ago (stopwatch gag).
Title card over the café: 'COULD 2 PEOPLE ACTUALLY REPOPULATE EARTH? ...seriously?', with REPOPULATE in colourful toy blocks. Music only, no narration.
The target is 8 billion. Best case for fertility: Hutterite women averaged ~10 kids (near the biological limit); the 69-children record is 'reportedly' and unverified (stamp gag).
Generous assumption of 8 kids per couple = x4 each generation: 2 -> 8 -> 32 -> 128, a family-tree pyramid with a ticking population counter, passing 8 billion in ~16 generations (~400 years). 'Easy.'
'Except there's a problem with generation two.' The camera pushes into the second row of the tree.

Life montage with year badges (Year 1 crib, Year 5 bunk bed, Year 12 so loud you sleep in the car, Year 20 dinner table). The grown kids look around for partners: the only young people are their siblings. Character: 'Oh, no.'

Why that's bad: genes come in pairs (spare-tire analogy). Everyone carries 1-2 hidden lethal mutations, so a random partner rarely matches but siblings share the same source. Data: ~3 in 10 children of the closest relatives died young or had a severe disability.

'History has already run this experiment': the Spanish Habsburgs married relatives to keep power. Charles II's inbreeding equalled a brother-sister child; he was sick, childless, and the dynasty ended in 1700.

Back in your world: +50/+75 years, grandkids are cousins, everyone is related to everyone. Each baby brings ~60 new mutations, most harmless, some not. Diversity is capped at 4 versions of any gene (toolbox analogy); low diversity means one disease could hit everyone.
Decades later the couple sit old on a porch at sunset watching their descendants and wonder whether they gave them a future 'or just a very slow ending.' A 1.4 s silence before it.

'But here's the thing, nature has squeezed through this exact gap before': the Chatham Islands black robin in 1980, 5 birds, 1 breeding pair (Old Blue & Old Yellow), cross-fostering of eggs, Old Blue lived to 14, now ~300 birds all descended from her, sharing the same weak spots, 'but they're here.'

More bottleneck survivors in quick succession: northern elephant seals ~20 -> 220,000+; Pitcairn Island's 27 settlers (1790) -> 193 descendants relocated by 1856; humans ourselves, ~1,280 breeding adults ~900,000 years ago for ~117,000 years (flagged as debated), 'could fit inside a high school gym.'

Answer: 'Technically, maybe.' Every species that made it paid a price, plus survivorship bias ('we only hear about the ones that made it'). Starship simulation: minimum crew 98, '49 times more people than you've got.' Character punchline: 'You should have made more friends.'
Personal question to the viewer: if it came down to you and one other person, who would you want next to you on that empty street? On-screen: 'WHO'S YOUR +1?' (comment bait).
~28 s music-only end screen: a blurred café background, a subscribe circle and two video cards, with the character sitting next to toy blocks that go from '2' to '98' while a robin lands next to him.

pacing.notes_on_speech: Conversational, unhurried read: about 144 wpm with regular music breathers. Only 3 pauses over 0.6 s, all at section turns (95.6, 118.5, 239.0 s).
pacing.rehook_interval_s: ~25-40 s. Each chapter opens with a turn line ('Except there's a problem...', 'Here's why that's bad', 'History has already run this experiment', 'But here's the thing...', 'So, could two people actually...'), and a new stat/counter or chip appears every 2-4 s.
pacing.structure_timing_pct: hook 0-9% | title 7-9% | best-case math 9-23% | problem reveal 23-28% | mechanism 28-40% | history proof 40-47% | escalation 47-62% | emotional low 59-62% | hope turn 62-72% | proof stack 72-83% | verdict + punchline 83-91% | CTA 91-93% | end screen 93-100%

techniques_worth_copying: One recurring 'you' couple as avatars: the viewer is cast as one of the 2 survivors, and they persist through every scene (café, chalkboard, home, porch), so abstract science becomes a personal story. Character voice lines ('So, it's just us?', 'Oh, no.', 'You should have made more friends.') are 1-line comic punctuation.
A home-base set with callbacks: the Corner Café opens, hosts the chalkboard math and closes the video, now full of people. The circular structure gives a satisfying ending.

Optimism first, then the catch: run the naive math to 'Easy.' ('16 generations, 400 years'), then pivot with 'Except there's a problem with generation two.' Building the viewer up before knocking them down drives retention.
A time-skip montage with calendar-tab badges (YEAR 1 / 5 / 12 / 20, +50 / +75 YEARS) and a gag insert (dad sleeping in the car) to show time passing in seconds.
Everyday analogies for mechanisms: spare tire = second gene copy; toolbox with 4 tools = gene diversity; high-school gym = 1,280 ancestors; '49 times more people than you've got'.
Comparison cards side by side (RANDOM PARTNER ✓ vs SIBLINGS ✗) on a dark blueprint-grid 'explainer void'. The style switches for abstract segments and comes back to the illustrated world for stories.

Counters everywhere: a dark box with a tiny uppercase label and a big number that tweens (POPULATION, NEW MUTATIONS, BLACK ROBINS LEFT, BREEDING ADULTS, N. ELEPHANT SEALS). Before/after number jumps are the visual payoff.

A credibility layer: a tiny source citation bottom-left on every stat, plus honest hedges on screen ('UNVERIFIED' stamp on the 69-kids record; '? debated: other scientists question the method'). It builds trust and invites 'well actually' comments.

Emotional low point at ~60% (old couple on the porch, 'a very slow ending'), then a hard hope turn ('But here's the thing, nature has squeezed through this exact gap before') into named-animal case studies (Old Blue and Old Yellow): named characters beat statistics.
Proof stack in the last third: 4 bottleneck survivors in ~85 s, each with its own set and a single counter, so the rhythm speeds up toward the verdict.

A nuanced verdict ('Technically, maybe') + survivorship-bias caveat + one hard number (98 minimum crew) + a joke punchline, then a personal comment question ('who would you want standing next to you?'; on screen 'WHO'S YOUR +1?').
A transition seed: a robin lands on the porch rail before the robin chapter, so objects carry the viewer between scenes instead of cuts.
SEO packaging: chapters in the description matching the beats, a sources list, long-tail tags for 'could 2 people repopulate earth' and 'minimum viable population'.

code_only_remake_requirements.feasibility: High. Everything is flat 2D vector art with gradients, so it can be rebuilt in Remotion with SVG components plus CSS/Canvas lighting effects. No footage or photoreal assets. The biggest cost is illustration volume (about 12 distinct sets), not animation complexity.
code_only_remake_requirements.character_rig: A 'bean' stick-figure SVG component: a black circle head with 2 big white eyes and pupils (look direction), optional brows/mouth for emotion (worried, surprised, happy), white hair tufts for the old version, thin black limb paths with simple walk/point/raise-arm/sit poses driven by interpolate(), and a coloured torso shape (tee, jacket, dress) as a prop. A palette of torso colours gives crowds of descendants. Needs walk cycles (2-4 key poses), blink, head-turn and sit-in-rocking-chair (rotation sway).
code_only_remake_requirements.sets_as_svg: Layered parallax scenes with 3-5 depth planes: street/café facade (awning stripes, windows, postbox, streetlamp), café interior with a chalkboard, pink living room, night car, navy blueprint-grid void, royal gallery (curtains, framed portraits), village street with bunting, sunset porch, island + sea, misty forest branches, beach, savanna silhouettes, gym bleachers, blurred end-screen background. Build each as a React SVG component with props for time of day.
code_only_remake_requirements.lighting_and_texture: Radial-gradient light pools and streetlamp bloom (SVG feGaussianBlur or CSS blur on additive shapes), diagonal volumetric light shafts (semi-transparent linear-gradient polygons with slow drift), film-grain overlay (an animated noise canvas at about 4% opacity), vignette, warm/cool colour grading via a full-frame gradient overlay with mix-blend-mode, and depth-of-field blur on background planes for the end screen.
code_only_remake_requirements.chalk_system: Chalk text and drawings: a handwritten font (e.g. Caveat or a similar OFL font) with stroke-dash write-on animation; chalk stick-figure icons duplicated for families; an SVG turbulence filter for chalk roughness; a board-wipe transition.
code_only_remake_requirements.data_viz_components: A counter box (label + tweened big number with thousands separators, plus a 'crash down' variant); a calendar-tab year badge; a caption 'pill' chip (rounded dark capsule, white text, bottom-centre, spring pop-in); a source citation line (tiny grey text bottom-left); a family-tree pyramid generator (n generations × branching factor, rows of tiny icons, auto-scaling); a gene bead columns component (2 columns of glowing circles, colour = parent, broken bead state); a comparison card with check/X; an icon row with red highlighting; a gauge meter; an 'UNVERIFIED' stamp slam (scale 2 -> 1 with rotation and shake).
code_only_remake_requirements.camera: A virtual camera wrapper (scale + translate on the scene group) with eased push-in/pull-out and truck moves, since most 'shots' are camera moves within one set, plus a focus-target helper for zooming into a tree row or portrait.
code_only_remake_requirements.transitions: Cross-dissolve, push-through zoom into a diagram, hard cut for before/after counters, a fade to desaturate for the disease beat, and object-carry transitions (the robin lands in one set, then cut to the island).
code_only_remake_requirements.audio: Local TTS narrator (Kokoro) at about 140-150 wpm with a calm, wry tone; a second and third voice for character one-liners (a different Kokoro voice); a soft ambient music bed (royalty-free or procedurally generated) under everything, with ducking; SFX for chalk scratch, stamp thud, counter ticks, bird chirps, crowd murmur.
code_only_remake_requirements.captions: None burned in (long-form 16:9). On-screen text is limited to chips, counters and labels. Captions only for a Shorts cut-down.
code_only_remake_requirements.storyboard_schema_needs: Per beat: set id, characters + poses + positions, camera keyframes, an overlay list (chip text, counter label/from/to, badge text, citation) with timing tied to narration word timestamps, and a transition type. A 7-minute video ≈ 45 shot entries ≈ 15-20 set components, which is reusable across what-if episodes (the café/street, explainer void and landscape kit generalise).
code_only_remake_requirements.render_cost_notes: Mostly static vector layers with transforms, so it is cheap to render. Blur filters and grain are the main cost: precompute blurred backgrounds as PNGs, or limit blur radius. Use 1920x1080 at 30 fps.
